findings.summary: The gh:: test would also pass under the old code unless its range includes commits that are not job landings.
findings.evidence: gh.rs:1421-1434 currently maps every PrCommit to LandingKind::JobLanding with Some(job) and a verification. If the gh:: test range holds only job-landing commits, the old mapping produces the same LandingCommit values and they pass validate. Fix: In the gh:: test, use a range that includes a records_only commit and a declared_intervention commit. Assert their kind, and assert job == None and verification == None, before calling LandingCommit::validate on each.

findings.summary: Refusing a commit that closes several jobs is a deliberate departure from the gate, which accepts squash chains (D69). The plan should state this and test it.
findings.evidence: The doc comment on landing_job at invariant.rs:205-206 says a valid landing is 'one job, or every job of a chain'. Under the plan, pr_commits would refuse a PR commit that the gate accepts. Fix: Add a short refusal test for a commit whose closing_jobs holds two jobs, asserting the error names the sha. State the limit in the pr_commits doc comment and in the change description, and name the follow-up: LandingCommit carries only one job.
findings.location: Decision 3 (more than one job in closing_jobs is an error)

findings.summary: Athena owns commits, so the producer cannot write and then inspect a commit body.
findings.evidence: The agent contract says Athena owns commits and history. Step 9 says 'write the commit body to match what was run', and the criterion 6 demonstration reads HEAD. Fix: Have the producer put the commit message body in the form its role requires (the commit message it hands back), with the same callers/writers list and commands as the CHANGELOG entry. Make the CHANGELOG entry the artifact a verifier can read in the diff.
findings.location: Step 9 and criterion 6 demonstration (`git show --stat HEAD`)

findings.summary: State whether an intervention record that is added but malformed still counts.
findings.evidence: The plan matches by path only, as the trailer-based intervention() does at invariant.rs:674-688. A path match on an unparsable record would classify the commit as declared_intervention. Fix: Say in the doc comment that matching is by path, mirroring the gate. Optionally require that the record parses.

summary: The plan matches the request and the accepted reading. It reproduces the content-based pr_commits, adds the missing change description listing callers and writers, and fixes the two earlier minor findings. I read the code it names, and it all exists as described: closing_jobs is private at crates/athena-gate/src/invariant.rs:225 and already leaves out jobs whose outcome is not landed. The trailer-based intervention helper is at :674. Change::of_commit and Judged::new are public in athena-gate lib.rs, and fingerprint is public in athena_git::attrs. athena-core already depends on athena-gate. LandingKind has RecordsOnly and DeclaredIntervention. pr_commits (land.rs:122) is called only from gh.rs GitLandingRecords::commits (gh.rs:1422), which today hard-codes JobLanding for every commit. So the change is made where the fault starts, and leaving run.rs and drain.rs unchanged is justified. The rule order (closing_jobs, then added intervention, then fingerprint-changed error, then records_only) gives the classifications that criteria 1–3 ask for. A blocked outcome drops out of closing_jobs, so a commit that adds a blocked outcome with governed work reaches the fingerprint refusal and fails with its sha. My findings are minor: one demonstration would not fail under the old mapping, the multi-job case needs to be stated, and the plan should not assume the producer makes the commit.
